## 6.226. ots-diagnostics

#### Command Description

This command is used to set or show the attributes associated with OTS diagnostics.

**Tip:** The **ots-diagnostics** name is auto generated by the system on line card provisioning. The format is 'ots-diagnostics-\<chassis\>-\<slot\>-\<DWDM Line\>'.

#### Command Syntax

```
set ots-diagnostics-<name> [nmoper-alarm-reporting <value>] [expected-operator <value>]
show ots-diagnostics-<name> [tti-style] [nmoper-alarm-reporting] [expected-operator] [tx-operator] [rx-operator] [tti-port-id]
```

#### Command Usage Details

**Table 541: ots-diagnostics Command Usage**

| Section | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Access Mode | Operational mode, Candidate Configuration mode |

#### Command Parameters

**Table 542: ots-diagnostics Command Parameters**

| Parameter | Description | Values | Default | Used in |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| name | The name of the diagnostic | string | &lt;chassis&gt;-&lt;slot&gt;-&lt;DWDM Line&gt; | show |
| nmoper-alarm-reporting | If enabled, the mismatch beween expected-operator and rx-operator parameters will raise the Neighbor-Mismatch Operator- Specific field (NMOPER) alarm. Disabling the NMOPER monitoring clears the NMOPER alarm immediately and disables the comparison. | • disabled<br>• enabled | disabled | set, show |
| monitoring-mode | The monitoring mode on the client. | intrusive | intrusive | set, show |
| tti-style | The configured mode of the TTI for this OTU/ODU client or OTS. tti-style in ots-diagnostics for all ots interfaces will implicitly change to 'proprietary' when NE's l0-mode-op is set to 'slte'. tti-style will revert to default value(ITU-T- G709) when NE's l0-mode-op is not set to 'slte'.<br>• ITU-T-G709 - TTI is split into SAPI, DAPI and OPER bytes.<br>• proprietary - TTI is a single 64 byte string. | • ITU-T-G709<br>• proprietary | ITU-T-G709 | show |
| rx-operator | The value of this attribute is used to allow the user to verify the NE connected on the other end of the fiber. The value is the trail trace identifier of the NE connected on the other end of the fiber, and is taken from the received OTS TTI Operator Specific bytes (carried in the OC3 OSC overhead). The value is by the far-end (remote) facility to the near-end (local) facility. It can be up to 32 characters/bytes. | tti-32 | the field is empty | show |
| tx-operator | The transmitted operator specific bytes. The value of tx-operator is transmitted to the NE connected on the other end of the fiber via the OTS TTI Operator Specific bytes (carried in the OC3 OSC OH). The maximum length of tx-operator is 32 characters/bytes. The tx-operator is automatically defaulted by the system with the format "&lt;ne-name&gt;-&lt;Dxx&gt;". | tti-32 | &lt;ne-name&gt;-D00 | show |
| expected-operator | The expected operator specific bytes. The value of this attribute is the expected trail trace identifier of the NE connected on the other end of the fiber. It is provisioned by the user and can be up to 32 characters/bytes. | tti-32 | the field is empty | set, show |
| tti-port-id | The port-id in OTS TTI is the AID of the port but limited to 32 printable characters. It is only applicable and visible when tti-style is 'proprietary'. tti-port-id is port AID string of the DWDM Line port for the associated degree/ direction. If tti-style is ITU-T-G709, tti-port-id will not be visible. | string (length 1.32) | n/a | show |

#### Examples

This example shows how to set up OTS diagnostics:

```
set ots-diagnostics
```

This example shows how to retrieve OTS diagnostics parameters from RD20TM DWDM line terminating an OTS section:

```
show ots-diagnostics-1-1-dwdm-line
```

This example shows how to retrieve OTS diagnostics parameters from C2ILASGH DWDM lines (Line 1 and Line 2) terminating an OTS section:

```
show ots-diagnostics-1-1-dwdm-line1
show ots-diagnostics-1-1-dwdm-line2
```
